title: Life Cycle of a Polar Bear

cues.text: Deep inside a snow drift in the dead of winter,
a mother polar bear gives birth to tiny, blind cubs no bigger than a guinea pig.
The snow den acts as a cozy blanket,
keeping the family safe from freezing Arctic winds while the cub nurses and grows strong.
By spring, the family breaks out of the den and travels onto the vast sea ice, which is the bear's true home.
For over two years, the cub stays by its mother's side,
learning the difficult art of hunting ringed seals for fat and energy.
Once old enough to hunt on its own, the young bear leaves its mother to live a solitary life across the frozen ocean.
Adult polar bears spend most of their lives alone, traveling hundreds of miles across the ice to hunt.
In the spring, adults meet to mate, and the female prepares for the long months ahead.
When winter returns, she digs a new snow den, and the remarkable Arctic life cycle begins all over again.
